title: Reactions - 123 school
heading: Reactions
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: What happens in a chemical reaction?
questions.a: The reactants disappear and new substances with different properties are formed

questions.q: Name two things that show that a chemical reaction has taken place
questions.a: For example: a gas is formed, a precipitate is formed, the colour changes, it gets warmer or colder, light is given off

questions.q: Is the melting of ice a chemical reaction?
questions.a: No, it is a change of state. They remain water molecules

questions.q: What happens to the atoms during a chemical reaction?
questions.a: They are arranged differently. No atoms are added and no atoms are lost

questions.q: What is on the left of the arrow in a reaction scheme?
questions.a: The reactants

questions.q: What is on the right of the arrow in a reaction scheme?
questions.a: The products

questions.q: You see a gas escaping during a reaction. Is that an observation or a conclusion?
questions.a: An observation: you can see it. That a new substance has been formed is a conclusion.

questions.q: Give the word equation for the decomposition of water, with state symbols
questions.a: water (l) → hydrogen (g) + oxygen (g)

questions.q: Give the word equation for sodium reacting with water (sodium hydroxide solution and hydrogen are formed)
questions.a: sodium (s) + water (l) → sodium hydroxide solution (aq) + hydrogen (g)

questions.q: What is a decomposition reaction?
questions.a: A reaction in which one reactant is split into several products

questions.q: What is a synthesis reaction?
questions.a: A reaction in which one new substance is made from two or more substances

questions.q: What is decomposition using electric current called?
questions.a: Electrolysis

questions.q: What is decomposition using heat called?
questions.a: Thermolysis

questions.q: What is decomposition using light called?
questions.a: Photolysis

questions.q: Which of these substances can you not decompose: oxygen, water, carbon dioxide or glucose?
questions.a: Oxygen (O<sub>2</sub>), because it is an element. You cannot decompose elements.

questions.q: Name three substances that you cannot decompose
questions.a: For example: all metals, oxygen (O<sub>2</sub>), nitrogen (N<sub>2</sub>), chlorine (Cl<sub>2</sub>), neon

questions.q: How do you test for hydrogen gas?
questions.a: With a burning splint: you hear a pop (a popping sound)

questions.q: How do you test for oxygen gas?
questions.a: With a glowing splint: it bursts into flame

questions.q: How do you test for carbon dioxide?
questions.a: With a burning splint: the flame goes out, or with limewater: it turns cloudy (white)

questions.q: Two gases are formed in the electrolysis of water. Which ones?
questions.a: Hydrogen and oxygen

questions.q: What is this an example of: CaCO<sub>3</sub> is heated and decomposes into CaO and CO<sub>2</sub>?
questions.a: Thermolysis

questions.q: What is step 1 of the step-by-step method for a reaction equation?
questions.a: Write down the reaction scheme in words

questions.q: What do you do in step 3 of the step-by-step method?
questions.a: Set up the atom balance: balance the equation with coefficients

questions.q: What do you do in step 4 of the step-by-step method?
questions.a: Simplify the reaction equation

questions.q: What do you put in front of a molecular formula to balance the atoms: a subscript or a coefficient?
questions.a: A coefficient. You must never change the subscript (the small number)

questions.q: Balance: H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → H<sub>2</sub>O
questions.a: 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O (left 4 H and 2 O, right 4 H and 2 O)

questions.q: Balance: N<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub> → NH<sub>3</sub>
questions.a: N<sub>2</sub> + 3 H<sub>2</sub> → 2 NH<sub>3</sub> (left 2 N and 6 H, right 2 N and 6 H)

questions.q: Balance: Mg + O<sub>2</sub> → MgO
questions.a: 2 Mg + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 MgO (left 2 Mg and 2 O, right 2 Mg and 2 O)

questions.q: Balance: Na + Cl<sub>2</sub> → NaCl
questions.a: 2 Na + Cl<sub>2</sub> → 2 NaCl

questions.q: Balance: H<sub>2</sub>O → H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub>
questions.a: 2 H<sub>2</sub>O → 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> (left 4 H and 2 O, right 4 H and 2 O)

questions.q: Balance: C + O<sub>2</sub> → CO
questions.a: 2 C + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 CO

questions.q: Is this equation balanced? 4 NH<sub>3</sub> + 5 O<sub>2</sub> → 4 NO + 6 H<sub>2</sub>O
questions.a: Yes: on the left and the right there are 4 N, 12 H and 10 O

questions.q: Is this equation balanced? H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → H<sub>2</sub>O
questions.a: No: on the left there are 2 O atoms and on the right 1 O atom

questions.q: Simplify: 4 H<sub>2</sub> + 2 O<sub>2</sub> → 4 H<sub>2</sub>O
questions.a: Divide all coefficients by 2: 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O

questions.q: In a closed container, 50 g of reactants react completely to form products. How many g of products are formed?
questions.a: 50 g, because the mass stays the same (law of conservation of mass)

questions.q: Which of these reactions is a decomposition reaction?
questions.a: 2 H<sub>2</sub>O → 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub>
